correctness.rationale: For every nonempty dual set F, fixing selected uv yields missing-incidence sets A,B; convex complement prohibits distinct a in A and b in B. Hence A or B empty gives full star (with extra nonincident selected edges prohibited by an induced selected P3), or A=B is a singleton. In the latter case, arbitrary n>=5 supplies two remaining labels and an explicit selected P3; n=4 gives exactly a selected triangle. Both star and exceptional triangle satisfy converse convexity, n=3 is complete. This logically exhaustive proof yields all counts and boundaries. Actual packaged BFS verifier enumerates all 33864 subsets for n=3..6 and checks 10019 additional sampled cases for n=7,8; finite tests are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The novelty-bearing infinite-family statement is the complete dual general-position classification of L(K_n) for every n>=5, not the pre-existing generic dual definition or the n=4 complete-multipartite exception. The 2024 primary full text establishes the convex-complement equivalence but does not calculate T_n. The 2023 same-object primary full text calculates the lower ordinary general-position invariant, not the dual variant; its maximal ordinary stars/triangles do not automatically pass complement convexity. The structure and enumerator are neither subsumed by the identified similar-publication implications nor by the prior archived forts work. Targeted search cannot logically guarantee unpublished or unindexed absence; residual bibliography risk is recorded.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalent results for dual GP of Johnson J(n,2), triangular graphs, or line graphs may exist; search absence does not prove priority.
The n=4 boundary is covered by complete-multipartite theory and is included only for accurate complete scope.

value.rationale: The complete classification for every n>=5 gives a strong nonhereditary dichotomy: the n full stars are the only nonempty solutions, at a single maximal size n-1, and the n-2 consecutive positive smaller cardinalities are absent. It resolves the whole solution space, exact enumerator, optimum multiplicity and all proper-subset obstructions in a natural strongly regular Johnson graph family; this is not a trivial restatement of ordinary GP extrema or a computation of arbitrary small examples.
